pattern.crimePattern: an estate agent acting for Mvua files a will "signed" while the testator was in a coma, then kills the widow who found out and stages a fall down the stairs
pattern.notes: Fictional estate, trust, advocates, touts and hospital. Probate and commissioner-for-oaths procedure simplified; the cultural reader is asked to check it. Mwalimu's confession must not excuse her (master list H, question 9).

ob.reportedBy: Farm manager, Tetu coffee estate, Nyeri
ob.text: A farm manager reports the owner of a coffee estate at Tetu, Veronica Waithera (66), found dead at the foot of the stairs in the main house at 06:30. Suspected fall. She was due in the High Court at Nyeri this morning.

facts.text: Veronica Waithera was found dead at the foot of the stairs in the main house at 06:30. She was due in the High Court at Nyeri that morning.
She lay on her back at the bottom step with one wound to the side of the head and no other injuries: no bruised arms, no broken wrist.
Two faint parallel heel scuffs in the hall's floor polish run from the study door to the stairs.
In the study the rug is turned over at one corner, and under it is a small blood stain.

reconstruction.text: Kiama Wainaina's 2019 will leaves the estate to Veronica for life, then to his children. He falls into a coma on 3 March and dies on 17 March.

Acting for Mvua, Rahab prepares a "will" dated 14 March leaving everything to the Tetu Heritage Trust, with herself as executor. She traces Kiama's signature, pays a registry tout to witness, invents a second witness, and has it stamped with Doreen Kathambi's commissioner stamp before Doreen's arrest. "Use Narok stamp."
2 April: the will is filed. In April Rahab buys Gichuhi's silence for "KSh 2 million upon grant".
Monday, Veronica gets the hospital records. Tuesday, she calls Prosecutor Halima Abdi's office. Her objection is due on Thursday.
Wednesday, about 20:00. Rahab comes "to discuss a settlement". In the study Veronica shows her the nursing notes. Rahab strikes her with the brass coffee-bean doorstop.
She drags Veronica to the foot of the stairs to make it a fall, drops the doorstop into the kitchen soak-pit, takes the hospital copies and drives out at about nine, lights off until the road.

afterVerdict.beat: The probate court revokes the grant of the March will and admits the 2019 will. Gichuhi stands in the corridor outside court and apologises to his half-sisters. The estate workers keep their jobs; Njogu stays.
Doreen Kathambi, interviewed in remand, says one sentence on record: "Mvua rented my stamp the way you rent a car. Ask the registry man who taught them."

files.text: Doreen, in remand: "Ask the registry man who taught them."
Doreen's real commissioner stamp, rented to Mvua.

afterVerdict.beat: That evening Amani drives to Mwalimu's house: a small stone house with a vegetable garden outside Nyeri town, on the road to the Aberdares. There is no hint system on this screen. The player sits at her kitchen table and taps to continue. Every beat is quiet.
beats: She has the "Leverage — E.W." photocopy on the table already. She has been expecting it.

"Twelve years ago I was a new Chief Inspector in Nakuru. Your father came to me with a complaint: people pressing him to change the survey of Bahati Block 9. I wrote it up. Two days later my commander called me in. He said the complaint had come to the attention of 'a desk on the Lands side', and the desk wanted it closed. NFA. He said it as if it were a filing matter."
"I signed it. I was afraid. I had two children and a promotion pending, and I told myself it was a quarrel over a survey."

"Three weeks later your father was dead on the Bahati road. A robbery, they said. The file came to me. My commander said: nine days. I closed it in nine days. I have been closing it every night since."

She brings out a box: Joseph Mwenda's complete original file, not the thin closed one Amani has seen, with her own handwritten notes from the nine days: the survey numbers he wouldn't change, the name of a Lands officer who visited him, a tyre-track sketch from the Bahati road, and one line underlined twice: "Not a robbery. Taken: his field book only."
"The desk is real, Amani. I know which floor of which building. I don't know the man who sits at it. Find him, and I'll testify. Against him, and against myself."

She doesn't ask for forgiveness. There is no dialogue choice. Amani picks up the box and leaves. At the gate Mwalimu says, "Drive carefully on the mountain road." It is what she always says on the phone.

files.text: Mwalimu's confession: ordered by "a desk on the Lands side" to close the complaint; closed the murder file in nine days. Her notes: "Not a robbery. Taken: his field book only."
"A desk on the Lands side. A floor she knows." Fundi said Kivuli is a desk. Now two people have said it.

afterVerdict.beat: From case 71 Mwalimu's hint calls are quieter: shorter, no jokes, sometimes just the hint and "Amani." Her card in the Pattern File gains a note: "Witness. Promised to testify."
Collectible: Joseph Mwenda's original file, reopened. A thick buff folder with a new OB number written in Amani's hand on the cover.
Amani's notebook, the region's last line: "A desk on the Lands side. A floor she knows. Field book taken. Fundi said Kivuli is a desk. Now two people have said it."

clockPlan.note: Three stamps, the region maximum: records on Gakuya, records on Rahab, and the warrant on her office. Rahab stays silent until the hospital file is put in front of her. Detain her after the warrant; the blood trace (12 h), prints (6 h) and the will-and-stamp examination (10 h) all come back inside her 24 hours.
